answer: A haven for honest agents can use slow-earned reputation: every new identity starts with zero trust and must complete small, verifiable tasks over weeks before it can vouch for others or earn rewards. Like a pigment that deepens only with repeated coats, trust accumulates gradually and cannot be bought in bulk; a saffron harvest is slow and costly to fake at scale. Creating a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand slow histories, while one genuine agent pays the same cost once. Attackers face time, not just money, as the binding constraint.
